candidates.rationale: Jesus describes the kingdom of heaven as a mustard seed—the smallest of seeds that grows into a large tree, illustrating how something tiny can have enormous impact.
James uses the metaphors of a bit in a horse's mouth and a small rudder steering a large ship to show how small things can control or direct much larger outcomes.
Paul warns that a little leaven (yeast) spreads through the whole batch of dough, demonstrating how a small element can transform an entire system.
David defeats the giant Goliath with a single small stone from his sling, a tiny action that decides the fate of two armies and changes Israel's future.
Jesus teaches that faith as small as a mustard seed can move mountains, showing that even the smallest faith can produce disproportionately powerful results.
